relationships.title: Additive Color Mixing
relationships.description: Red Light combines with Green Light to create Yellow Light through additive color mixing - the foundation of RGB displays.

relationships.title: Primary to Secondary
relationships.description: Red Light is a primary component of Yellow Light, which appears when red and green wavelengths combine.

relationships.title: Primary to Secondary
relationships.description: Green Light is a primary component of Yellow Light, demonstrating how additive color mixing works in light.

relationships.title: Cyan Formation
relationships.description: Green Light combines with Blue Light to create Cyan Light, one of the secondary colors in additive mixing.

relationships.title: Primary to Secondary
relationships.description: Green Light is a primary component of Cyan Light, formed when green and blue wavelengths combine.

relationships.title: Primary to Secondary
relationships.description: Blue Light is a primary component of Cyan Light, visible when blue and green wavelengths merge.

relationships.title: Magenta Formation
relationships.description: Red Light combines with Blue Light to create Magenta Light, completing the RGB secondary color trio.

relationships.title: Primary to Secondary
relationships.description: Red Light is a primary component of Magenta Light, formed when red and blue wavelengths combine.

relationships.title: Primary to Secondary
relationships.description: Blue Light is a primary component of Magenta Light, visible when blue and red wavelengths merge.

relationships.title: RGB Primaries
relationships.description: Red and Green are two of the three primary colors of light, essential for creating all visible colors.

relationships.title: RGB Primaries
relationships.description: Red and Blue are two of the three primary colors of light, fundamental to color reproduction.

relationships.title: RGB Primaries
relationships.description: Green and Blue are two of the three primary colors of light, used in all digital displays.

relationships.title: RGB Triad
relationships.description: Red, Green, and Blue together form the RGB color model used in all digital screens and displays.

relationships.title: Dispersion
relationships.description: White Light splits through a Prism into its component colors, revealing the hidden spectrum within.

relationships.title: Light Separation
relationships.description: A Prism creates a Spectrum by separating white light into its constituent wavelengths and colors.

relationships.title: Full Color Range
relationships.description: White Light contains the entire Spectrum of visible colors, from red to violet wavelengths.

relationships.title: Natural Dispersion
relationships.description: The Spectrum manifests as a Rainbow when sunlight disperses through water droplets in the atmosphere.

relationships.title: Long Wavelength
relationships.description: Wavelength determines color - Red Light has the longest wavelength in the visible spectrum (~700nm).

relationships.title: Short Wavelength
relationships.description: Wavelength determines color - Blue Light has a shorter wavelength in the visible spectrum (~450nm).

relationships.title: Pixel Component
relationships.description: An RGB Pixel emits Red Light from its red subpixel to create red hues on digital displays.

relationships.title: Pixel Component
relationships.description: An RGB Pixel emits Green Light from its green subpixel, essential for display color reproduction.

relationships.title: Pixel Component
relationships.description: An RGB Pixel emits Blue Light from its blue subpixel, completing the RGB display technology.

relationships.title: LED Emission
relationships.description: LEDs produce Red Light through electroluminescence, used in displays and lighting.

relationships.title: Coherent Light
relationships.description: A Laser emits pure Red Light as coherent, monochromatic radiation at a specific wavelength.

relationships.title: Light Particle
relationships.description: A Photon carries energy at a specific Wavelength, determining the color of light we perceive.

relationships.title: Light Quantum
relationships.description: Photons constitute Red Light, each carrying energy corresponding to red wavelengths.
